proposals: The Department of Commerce should publish the full year-by-year wine tariff staging schedule agreed in the India–EU trade deal, for premium and mid-range wine separately, so that the phase-down from 150% to 75% and then to 20% or 30% is not reconstructed from trade press.

APEDA should publish an annual official count of wineries, wine-grape acreage and wine output by state, replacing the reliance on trade estimates for Nashik’s 45–50 wineries, Karnataka’s regional breakdown and the 1–2% of vineyard area grown for wine; the 2022 PIB count is the only government figure available.

The Maharashtra and Karnataka state excise departments should publish annual wine sales volumes, split into domestic and imported wine, so that per-capita consumption and wine’s share of alcohol volume can be stated from official data instead of a 0.5–2% triangulated range.

DGCI&S should publish monthly wine import volumes and values by origin country and price band before and after the EU deal takes effect, so that the question this piece says matters most — whether import volumes actually move — can be answered directly.

The Tamil Nadu Horticulture Department should report grape area and production by end use (table, raisin, wine) for Theni and other districts, so that the state’s move towards wine production can be tracked from official figures rather than one winery’s stated capacity.
